newsitem.title: USA: Sham medal winner publishes Memorial Day apology.
newsitem.headline: Sham medal winner publishes Memorial Day apology.

text.p: A Florida man who for years claimed he had won the Medal of Honour, the highest U.S military decoration, for his actions in the Korean War published a letter on Monday apologising for his "pitiful" behaviour.
Jackie Stern of Bonaventure, Florida, was found guilty in September 1996 of wearing the medal without authorisation. Part of his sentence was to publish an apology on Memorial Day.

"I know that my actions have cheapened the honour of those who have received this valiant award and my pitiful attempt and selfish quest for family recognition has tarnished the dignity of all the brave men and women on whom this medal was legitimately bestowed," he said in the letter, which appeared in the Sun-Sentinel.

Stern, who served in the Army during the Korean War but never saw combat, bought the medal at a New Jersey flea market. He became a well-known figure in his community, regaling listeners with tales of how he was wounded in action.
He said he wanted to win his children's respect by portraying himself as a war hero. Instead he had disgraced himself, humiliated his family and embarrassed his friends, he said.

"I love my country and those who have valiantlty served her through the armed forces ... please do not let the lies and deceptions of one old man tarnish the recognition and respect that should be given to veterans of the armed forces," Stern said.

The U.S. District Court also ordered Stern to write a personal letter of apology to all 169 living recipients of the Medal of Honour and volunteer for 250 hours in a Veterans Administration Hospital as part of his punishment.
